standard_prerequisites.name: The differentials of a product as a direct sum

standard_prerequisites.use: It identifies $\Omega_{X \times_S Y/S}$ with the direct sum $p^*\Omega_{X/S} \oplus q^*\Omega_{Y/S}$, which is the input to the degreewise computation.

standard_prerequisites.name: Elementary properties of exterior powers and the definition of the box product
standard_prerequisites.use: Taking exterior powers gives $\Omega^n_{X \times_S Y/S} = \bigoplus_{i+j=n} \Omega^i_{X/S} \boxtimes \Omega^j_{Y/S}$, matching the terms of the total complex.

core_obligations: Use the description of the differentials of a product as a direct sum of the pullbacks of the two factors' differentials (proof lines 882-886).

Take exterior powers and apply the elementary multiplicativity to obtain the decomposition $\Omega^n_{X \times_S Y/S} = \bigoplus_{i+j=n} \Omega^i_{X/S} \boxtimes \Omega^j_{Y/S}$, giving the termwise isomorphisms of the complexes (proof lines 887-896).
Note that the compatibility of these maps with the differentials is left to the reader (proof lines 896-898).
proof_roadmap: Exterior powers and the termwise identification (proof lines 887-896).
Compatibility with differentials left to the reader (proof lines 896-898).
difficulty_reason: The lemma identifies the de Rham complex of a product with the total complex of the exterior box product of the de Rham complexes of the factors (statement lines 870-879). The proof recalls the direct sum decomposition of the differentials of a product, takes exterior powers to obtain the degreewise decomposition, and notes that the resulting termwise isomorphisms are compatible with the differentials. The degreewise computation is the substance, so the claim is H2.
